name: Scandinavism
summary: Scandinavism is the 19th-century movement for closer unity among the Danes, Swedes and Norwegians, resting on shared Old Norse heritage, mythology and closely related languages. Its cultural wing built joint literary and student networks, while its political wing, centred on Danish National Liberals, sought anything from a military alliance to a confederation or a union under one Bernadotte king, largely as a defence against Russia and Prussia. It collapsed when Sweden-Norway did not aid Denmark in 1864, but its cultural side fed the monetary union of 1873 and later Nordic cooperation.
scope: The mid-19th-century Scandinavist movement (c. 1840s to 1864) as documented in the student meetings, the Danish National Liberals (Carl Ploug, Orla Lehmann) and Swedish-Norwegian royal sympathisers (Oscar I, Carl XV), plus the cultural Scandinavism that persisted afterward. It excludes modern Nordic cooperation as a programme, except as legacy. Because the movement had little economic or social policy, most answers on those topics are low-confidence inferences from its bourgeois-liberal base.

keyFigures.name: Carl Ploug
keyFigures.role: Danish National Liberal editor and poet whose 1842 song became a battle song of Scandinavism.

keyFigures.name: Charles XV of Sweden
keyFigures.role: Swedish-Norwegian king who championed a Nordic union and promised Denmark aid in 1863.

keyFigures.name: Hans Christian Andersen
keyFigures.role: Poet of 'Jeg er en Skandinav' (1839), intended as part of a Scandinavian anthem.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed in the 1840s-60s movement; the Nordic welfare states are a later legacy, and the movement itself held no health policy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Mid-19th-century liberal nationalists had no wage-setting programme; inferred from the era's liberal wariness of state wage regulation.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: National Liberal supporters were bourgeois liberals of their era; inferred, since the movement's own concerns were cultural and dynastic rather than economic.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the movement concerns nationalising industry; inferred from its middle-class liberal base.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The movement never addressed taxation; nothing in its middle-class base points either way.

unions-good.rationale: Pre-dates organised labour in Scandinavia; its students and bourgeois liberals took no stance on unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred from the bourgeois liberal milieu of the National Liberals who carried the political wing; property was not a movement theme.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Joint-stock regulation was not a movement issue; no basis to lean either way.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not an issue in the 19th century; mildly inferred from the later Nordic cooperation tradition that grew from the movement and accommodates welfare states.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not a concern of a student and bourgeois liberal movement; inferred as opposed to cooperative socialism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement said nothing on security versus privacy.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the moderately conservative 19th-century bourgeois mainstream.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anachronistic; its liberals campaigned for press freedom against absolutism (Ploug edited the liberal Faedrelandet), so a speech-restricting law is unlikely.

strong-leader.rationale: The political wing sat in the liberal opposition to absolute monarchy and favoured constitutional government, opposing a leader bypassing parliament.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement aimed to create or enlarge states (a union or confederation of the Nordic kingdoms), so abolishing the state is contrary to it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Scandinavists wanted stronger mutual defence against Russia and Prussia, so inferred support for stronger defence forces; police not addressed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the moral conservatism of the 19th-century bourgeois milieu.

decide-locally.rationale: Its aim was supranational union above the national states, and in Denmark the National Liberals centralised toward Schleswig; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy was not a movement concern.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's conventional bourgeois norms (Ploug later opposed women's suffrage).

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from 19th-century norms, though adherents today would likely differ.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion was a minor theme; clergy joined cross-border meetings, but the movement was mainly secular-romantic.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural Scandinavism promoted shared Nordic heritage, mythology and literature and joint cultural societies, so cultural preservation is central, though framed as a shared rather than separate national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement sought sweeping unification yet advanced it through meetings, literature and diplomacy; adherents split between cautious cultural and activist political wings.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration was not an issue in this period.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: It sought a supranational Nordic union or confederation, and its legacy is the Nordic Council; global organisations did not exist, so this is inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Its cultural cooperation fed the Scandinavian monetary union of 1873 and economic integration; the National Liberals were 19th-century free-trade liberals, though not a movement theme.

nation-first.rationale: A smaller-state alliance against larger neighbours, appealing to Nordic solidarity over narrow national interest; Sweden-Norway's refusal in 1864 is what adherents criticised.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement sought military aid to Denmark but not for human rights.

open-borders.rationale: It favoured closer Nordic ties and later free movement among Nordic states, but not open borders generally.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from 19th-century liberal progress optimism; not a movement theme.

revolution-justified.rationale: It grew within liberal reform politics and sought union through monarchs and diplomacy rather than revolution, though 1848 liberal upheaval surrounded it.

experts-over-public.rationale: Led by scholars, poets and students yet liberal in politics; adherents not clearly split on this.

central-planning.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal bourgeois base.

socialized-markets.rationale: The movement had no view on enterprise ownership, and the question is a later socialist-market debate, so no lean can be inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Georgist tax reform came after the movement and was never part of its cultural or dynastic agenda.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation was not debated by the student and liberal circles, and nothing in their aims points either way.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Liberal economic outlook and the move toward monetary union lean against tariffs; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal base.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Peasant landholding was a romantic theme at folk festivals, but no property doctrine is documented for the movement.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Utterly foreign to a bourgeois-liberal national movement; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The 1873 monetary union it helped prepare used central banks; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; liberal base, so opposed to state-recognised corporatist bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Its political supporters were the parliamentary liberal opposition to absolutism and fought for constitutional government, so single-party rule is contrary.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Carl XV and Oscar I backed the plan of a Nordic union under one Bernadotte king, and the 1863 hopes rested on the 'brotherly kings'; monarchy was the accepted vehicle, though its liberal wing wanted constitutional limits.

democracy-best.rationale: The Danish political wing was liberal and opposed absolutism; Ploug began as a champion of universal male suffrage, but democracy was not the movement's defining aim.

direct-votes.rationale: Mid-19th-century liberals favoured representative assemblies, not referendums; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Danish Scandinavists fought the Schleswig-Holstein separatism and backed the Eider policy, so secession of regions was resisted.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; royal sympathisers and liberal critics of aristocratic privilege coexisted.

political-violence-never.rationale: It sought Swedish-Norwegian military aid and volunteers in the Schleswig wars, so war was acceptable; individual political violence not addressed.

war-builds-character.rationale: Romantic nationalists valued martial Nordic tradition and volunteers fought in 1848-50, but no doctrine states this.

separate-church-state.rationale: Nordic states had Lutheran state churches throughout and the movement did not challenge this; inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Liberal and secular-romantic in orientation; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: It was a state-building movement seeking collective defence; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Small states sought safety through alliance against Russia and Prussia, not superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: It treated Danes, Swedes and Norwegians as kin of common Old Norse descent and a shared mythology, so kinship-based identity is central, though it spans three nations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Not a class-based ideology; inferred from its national-liberal outlook.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal base.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed (the Sami were not part of its agenda).

colonial-reparations.rationale: The question is anachronistic, since the movement concerned intra-Nordic unity rather than overseas colonialism.

civilizational-union.rationale: Scandinavists held that peoples of shared Old Norse heritage, language and culture should draw together, the ideology's core claim, though the basis was kinship and language more than religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; the movement appealed to solidarity but also to mutual security interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Its liberal wing fought absolutism for constitutional rights, so rights were not subordinated to duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Romantic Nordic mythology valued nature but no political position on intrinsic value is documented.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the progress-minded liberal outlook.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technology was not a theme, though scientist meetings such as Gothenburg 1839 show interest in progress without a stance on disruption.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from liberal parliamentary orientation.

restore-past-order.rationale: It aimed at a new union and was liberal-progressive, though it also drew on a romantic idealised Nordic past; the revival of the past was cultural, not social restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed; adherents argued from romantic ideals and from realpolitik alike.

direct-action.rationale: It worked through student meetings, journals, elections and diplomacy, with volunteers in war only as a one-off; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Neither its cultural wing nor its diplomatic wing stated a principle linking methods to the intended society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Foreign to its modernising romantic-national outlook; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal base.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from bourgeois liberal base.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; its war explanation was Russian and German power politics.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from its National Liberal wing, whose liberalism favoured civil liberties against absolutism.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stressed peoples, a collective, while its liberal wing stressed individual rights.

conscription.rationale: The movement sought strong mutual defence, and Danish liberals supported conscription of the 1848 war era; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: It stressed voice and union, not exit; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: The philosophical distinction was not part of its liberal-national discourse, so no position can be inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Its main force was students, scholars and newspapers, yet the claim is a modern one that adherents did not make.

total-state.rationale: Liberal opposition to absolutism makes this contrary.

national-rebirth.rationale: Romantic revival of the Nordic heritage and mythology implied a renewal of Nordic identity, but not a doctrine of decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Aim was union, not conquest; but Danish Scandinavists defended Schleswig claims. Genuinely mixed.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; contrary to its liberal constitutionalism.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Anachronistic; romantic nationalists did use scholarship (philology, archaeology) to claim Nordic unity, treating it as objective.

universal-morality.rationale: The movement offered no moral philosophy, only a shared cultural identity for Nordic peoples.

single-common-good.rationale: It sought a common Nordic good in unity, but with competing liberal, royalist and literary strands it did not hold a doctrine of one rationally found good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Unrelated to Nordic unity, and no document of the movement addresses Zionism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The movement did not address diaspora return, and Nordic free movement came only later.

revive-national-language.rationale: Cultural Scandinavism emphasised the shared linguistic heritage and joint journals promoting Nordic languages; this is a loose fit for revival of an unused language, hence low.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance was not on the agenda of a student and cultural movement, so no lean is inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from 19th-century liberal fiscal orthodoxy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred from the National Liberal milieu; not a movement theme.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; liberal wing preferred constitutional law.

national-self-determination.rationale: It was a national-liberal movement drawing on the same romantic nationalism as German and Italian unification, and defended the Danish-speaking north of Schleswig; though its goal was a wider union of three nations.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Romantic nationalism valued mythology and emotion alongside scholarship.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nothing in the movement concerns welfare eligibility, though later Nordic cooperation treats Nordic citizens alike.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality was not an issue in the 1840s-60s, and the movement is silent on it.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bourgeois and student movement seeking national unity above class; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage was the movement's central object.

workers-nation.rationale: The movement was cross-class and national rather than working-class, so the statement does not map onto it.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from 19th-century norms; Ploug opposed women's suffrage.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; contrary to its commercial liberal base.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed; its kinship concept was cultural and linguistic.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for a mid-19th-century movement, so nothing can be inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration to the Nordic states was negligible in the period, and the movement had no stance on assimilation.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral-system design was not debated in its sources, though liberals favoured elected assemblies generally.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; some Scandinavists saw a Nordic cultural calling, but not a mission to spread government.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Liberals criticised absolutist rule, but the movement made no general corruption charge against political elites.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past killings is a modern issue that the movement never addressed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Not addressed; liberal base but state-building aims.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No documented stance; its kinship concept was cultural and linguistic among related Nordic peoples, so mild disagreement is inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrinal question with no connection to a Nordic national-cultural movement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement did not address settler states, and the Nordic union plans involved no settlement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred; the Nordic cooperation tradition aims at uniform laws among the Nordic states, though not about religion.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religion was marginal to it, and inferred from liberal freedoms that conversion would not be restricted by law.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No part of the Nordic cultural or political programme could support a ban on slaughter, a question from Indian politics.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Soviet-style doctrine unrelated to Scandinavism, so neutral by default.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Its liberal wing sought constitutional government by popular consent against absolute monarchs.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade balance was not discussed in its sources, so there is no basis for a lean.

population-transfer.rationale: Nothing in its documented programme proposes removing minorities, and its handling of Schleswig was about borders and allegiance, so mild disagreement is inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; it sought military action in the Schleswig wars.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Romantic nationalists celebrated Nordic strength, but the movement preached cooperation among peoples, not struggle as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans were not an issue in the period, and the movement offered no view.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Liberal opposition to absolutism echoes the idea, but the republican theory was not part of the movement's discourse.

separated-powers.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism of the National Liberals; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist theory is foreign to a liberal student and cultural movement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Poverty relief was not its concern, and no source reports a view.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A 20th-century British housing policy with no bearing on the movement.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Industrial relations law postdates the movement, so no lean can be inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malthusian debates were not part of the movement's agenda.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed; its premise was that kinship eases cooperation.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's liberals favoured elected assemblies, so sortition is mildly opposed by inference.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; its liberal wing prized constitutional protections but backed wartime measures in the Schleswig wars, so it is left split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the free-market leaning of its bourgeois liberal supporters.

party-controls-media.rationale: Press freedom was central to the National Liberals (Ploug edited Faedrelandet).

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the military is foreign to its monarchical and constitutional framework, where the king commanded forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules were not discussed by the movement.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: MP pay was not a movement issue, and nothing indicates a view.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Modern party discipline did not exist in the movement's era, so no lean can be drawn.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Visions ranged from a confederation to a union under a common king; its legacy the Helsinki Treaty and the Nordic Council, so pooling sovereignty among Nordic states is central.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Carl XV pledged troops personally, but the Swedish-Norwegian government overruled him, and adherents differed on constitutional limits.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Nordic Lutheran churches were state-run, and church governance did not feature in the movement.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clergy has no place in a secular-romantic and liberal-parliamentary movement.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; Scandinavists wanted supporting Denmark in war.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term limits were not an issue for a movement oriented to monarchies.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials was not a feature of its constitutional liberalism.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The movement sought alliance, from a confederation to a military alliance at minimum, against Russia and Prussia.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Property-owning liberals had no wish to ban renting, and the idea has no source in the movement.

people-in-arms.rationale: Volunteers fought in 1848-50, but it did not argue for replacing professional forces with a militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Romantic nationalists idealised peasants, folk festivals at Himmelbjerget and Skamlingsbanken, but no stance recorded.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Scandinavism aimed at closer unity of the Nordic peoples, framed by some as reuniting a historic Nordic whole; not a formal border dispute.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement was led by students, poets and scholars; inferred that adherents would reject this.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; its stress on Nordic distinctiveness vs Germans did not rank cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment was not addressed by the movement, and Nordic opinion in the period was itself shifting.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from 19th-century bourgeois norms, so mild disagreement.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's scholars were philologists and archaeologists but took no stance on school science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed by the movement and no inference from its aims is safe.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Its kinship rhetoric stressed shared ancestry, but it did not discuss citizenship law.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; Danish Schleswig language questions were a flash point, but not framed that way.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious minorities were a marginal issue for the movement.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument was not part of the movement, which prized shared national feeling.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the fiscal conservatism of its liberal base.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Its aims were political and cultural, with no demand for economic transformation.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Its liberals fought for freedoms against absolutism, so trading them for growth would be foreign.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid is anachronistic for the period, so no view can be inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Its plans centred on dynastic union under a Bernadotte king.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anachronistic; monetary union is documented but not central-bank design.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Danish Scandinavists defended Schleswig but did not address territory-for-peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: It had no doctrine of property, so any stance would be invented.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate within Marxism that the movement never touched.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the movement's sources.

collective-defense.rationale: A military alliance was the minimum Scandinavist goal; Carl XV signed a defence treaty with Denmark in 1863, and Danish hopes of Swedish-Norwegian aid drove the Schleswig politics.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed; Danes disputed the Prussian-Austrian annexation of the duchies, but this was not framed as occupation law.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: It left the Nordic state churches as they were and said nothing about curbing them.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the king-centred union plans, in which the monarch is a unifying symbol.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Danish Scandinavists backed the Eider policy and the wars of 1848-51 and 1864 to hold Schleswig.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Norway kept its own constitution under the 1814 union, a model for union with autonomy, but no stated position.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contrary to the liberal wing; not documented.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income taxation was not debated by the movement and nothing suggests a view.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement's romantic idea of inherited Nordic character sits against environmentalism, but no source resolves it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Its political wing was the liberal opposition to absolutism in Denmark.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and wholly outside the movement's concerns.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Its monarchical and liberal strands implied a blended constitution, but the movement never stated a theory of mixed rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Mass praise of a leader is absent from its documentation, and its liberal wing opposed personal rule.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is a modern issue and no part of the movement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrinal question with no bearing on Scandinavism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its property-owning liberal base, so mild opposition.

refugee-return.rationale: The movement did not address refugee return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Danish Scandinavists defended Danish-speaking Schleswig, but the Nordic kin claim was for union, not claiming territory.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy contradicts the liberal freedoms of its political wing.

women-must-cover.rationale: Nothing in Nordic liberal or cultural nationalism supports legal dress mandates, so strong disagreement is inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Cultural Scandinavism helped prepare the Scandinavian monetary union of 1873-1914, in which Denmark, Sweden and later Norway shared a currency standard.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Core idea: peoples sharing language, ancestry and Old Norse heritage should unite, from a confederation to a kingdom of Scandinavia.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: It addressed cultural union of three peoples, not minority autonomy, so no position is documented.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not applicable to a movement of majority peoples.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Idealist romantic movement driven by culture, scholarship and ideas; not materialist.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy came after the movement and is not addressed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are anachronistic for the period, and nothing allows a lean.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; liberal constitutionalism leans to checks.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; economic cooperation was among Nordic states, with no closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Modern trade-treaty standards are anachronistic; Nordic cooperation harmonises laws but this is not documented as a movement position.

moral-incentives.rationale: Maoist-style moral incentives have no analogue in the movement, so mild disagreement is inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foquismo is foreign to a constitutional-liberal movement that sought union through kings and diplomacy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Backed monarchy, and liberals attacked absolutism, not the nobility specifically; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: It promoted a shared Nordic past and mythology in education and literature.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial tutelage was not part of a movement about unity of related Nordic peoples.

patriotic-education.rationale: Andersen's poem was written to be a Scandinavian anthem and it fostered song, flag and heritage; patriotic education is inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic and unrelated to the movement.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its liberal base and the central-bank-based monetary union of 1873.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A Marxist-revisionist question beyond the movement's scope.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; the Nordic kingdoms were former rivals, now partners.

delink-world-market.rationale: Delinking is a 20th-century theory, and the movement's union plans were pro-integration among Nordic states.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory irrelevant to the movement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred only from mild liberal egalitarianism, so low-confidence disagreement.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Norway's 1814 constitution is noted; no stated position.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: No documented view on colonial treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Plans involved succession by a Bernadotte king and Ploug's 1856 proposal that the Swedish crown prince succeed Frederik VII.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: National Liberals opposed absolutism and favoured constitutional rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from the National Liberals' constitutional liberalism.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristocratic duty was not a theme in its documentation.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: An activist political and cultural movement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A 20th-century critical-theory claim, which the movement, relying on cultural mobilisation, would reject.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory has no connection to the movement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim foreign to the movement; mild disagreement inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed, but Nordic cooperation implied cross-border access.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question not applicable to Scandinavism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development aid is anachronistic and was not addressed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Danish Scandinavists wanted to hold Schleswig; the lost Finland issue was not framed as a demand.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; the Sami were outside the movement's concerns.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascism postdates the movement, so no stance can be drawn.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: A 20th-century comparison that postdates the movement.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historiographical dispute unrelated to Scandinavism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no basis for a lean.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: A modern gender-policy debate that the movement never took up.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: A modern debate that the movement never addressed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The movement did not debate cultural relativism of institutions.

paid-care-work.rationale: Anachronistic; unpaid household labour was not discussed.

filial-duty.rationale: Family ethics were not part of its programme.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service selection was not discussed in its sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the movement's documents.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandates conflict with the representative assemblies its liberals favoured, so mild disagreement is inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is an anachronistic matter that the movement never considered.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal land tenure is foreign to its property-owning liberal base, so mild disagreement is inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: A core demand of liberal constitutionalism against absolute monarchy; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: It stressed the dialect continuum of North Germanic languages and joint Scandinavian languages, not a single state language; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; Nordic cooperation sought cross-border ties.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A modern anti-discrimination doctrine unrelated to the movement.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement said nothing about consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Its war aim was open military alliance with Denmark, not covert support for insurgents, so mild disagreement is inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; the union ideal was voluntary.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign finance are anachronistic and unmentioned.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Its kinship idea rested on language, mythology and shared descent, but there is no documented claim about group ability, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: National Liberals sat in the Danish Constituent Assembly of 1848 (Ploug among them), so an elected assembly to write a constitution fits their politics.

minority-veto.rationale: Its plans needed majority agreement among states and monarchs, and it did not argue for veto powers; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed in the 1840s-60s movement; cross-border Nordic ties implied no case for or against limiting foreign money.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The movement had no population policy; nothing in the sources supports either side.

residents-only-property.rationale: Its bourgeois-liberal base favoured free property markets; inferred, not stated.

job-guarantee.rationale: Mid-19th-century liberals held that jobs come from the market; inferred from the movement's base.

democratic-peace.rationale: Danish National Liberals were liberal-constitutional in outlook, from which a belief that liberal states keep peace is inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Liberal constitutionalists held that law binds as a legitimate, constitutional order; inferred, not stated.

non-intervention.rationale: Its goal was a mutual defence alliance, and it saw Prussian action against Denmark as illegitimate, so it would not take a rule of absolute non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Pre-dates industrial unions; the sources give no view on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The movement rested on kinship among three peoples and no minority plot is documented; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the era's liberal and Lutheran norms; no source suggests ending legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-constitutional base and the Nordic tradition of open government; not stated in the sources.

local-production.rationale: The movement's legacy was economic integration, the 1873 monetary union, which points away from local-only production.

informal-organisation.rationale: It worked through student meetings and societies yet also sought a formal union, so adherents were split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Its political wing sought a confederation or union of the Nordic states, which implies shared authority above national law.

religious-nation.rationale: Scandinavist unity was based on Old Norse heritage, language and kinship, not on a shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The movement sought equal kin kingdoms united against Russia and Prussia, not tribute to a hegemon; inferred from its alliance and union aims.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; the movement had no fiscal programme, and union plans leave the question of regional budgets open.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from the movement's bourgeois-liberal base, which defended private property; common ownership of production was not on its agenda.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism as a state system did not exist in the 1840s-60s; the movement's foe was Russian and Prussian power, so no position can be inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from the National Liberal outlook, which favoured voluntary association and private initiative alongside public institutions; not stated.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Romantic revival of Old Norse myth and its Lutheran, monarchist backers, who did not treat religion as an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed; liberal adherents valued commerce and progress but the movement did not judge capitalism as a historical stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the mid-century liberal view that legal and educational reform, not economic transformation, would improve social conditions.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the era's bourgeois family norms; public domestic services were not a concern of the movement.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The cultural wing stressed the closeness of the Danish, Swedish and Norwegian languages and joint literary ties, not purging foreign words; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the movement concerned treaties and alliances between kingdoms, not with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from its monarchist and liberal-nationalist base, which kept existing kingdoms and property rather than communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: The movement sought union of existing peoples, not settlement of one group in another's regions; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred from its liberal base; it aimed at a Nordic union, not at a third economic system between capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The movement rested on shared Old Norse heritage and the National Liberals' Schleswig claims, so historical ties counted; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement predates the Holocaust, so this is inferred from its liberal outlook.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic: mid-19th-century Nordic law criminalised it and the bourgeois-liberal movement did not challenge that; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Its Danish National Liberal core, with Ploug's Faedrelandet, campaigned for free press, assembly and constitutional government.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Liberal supporters favoured religious toleration in principle, though state churches stayed; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement had no colonial programme and Denmark held colonies, so adherents are not clearly for or against; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not relevant to a Nordic movement; no stated position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Constitutional liberals and monarchs alike had no religious-law legitimacy test; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: National Liberals favoured representative government rather than direct participation; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement had no social-structural analysis of this kind; inferred from its liberal base.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic: not a mid-19th-century concern; inferred from the era's bourgeois-liberal outlook.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic: not a concern of the movement; inferred from the era's norms.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; the movement united cultural romantics and political liberals and monarchs.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx-style critique was outside the movement's bourgeois-liberal base; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; Islam was not a concern of the 1840s-60s movement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Liberals favoured constitutional rule though Scandinavist monarchs relied on the Crown; inferred, adherents mixed.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed by the movement.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed by the movement.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement held no economic programme; the welfare-state tradition is a later legacy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Its political wing sought military alliance or union against Russia and Prussia, and the 1863 defence treaty shows reliance on armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; the movement had no development programme.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: It sought a Nordic military alliance against Russia and Prussia, so adherents wanted alignment, not neutrality, though only within the Nordic group.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The movement relied on hereditary monarchs, notably a union under one Bernadotte king with Oscar I and Carl XV, so child succession was taken for granted.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed by a mid-19th-century cultural and military unity movement; no position is documented.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anachronistic: no international lender conditions existed in the movement's period, and its liberal base gave no stance.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from the bourgeois-liberal National Liberals, who accepted the restricted suffrage of their era; the sources do not discuss it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Anachronistic ecofeminist idea; the movement had no position.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to the bourgeois-liberal movement; rejection is inferred from its base.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the National Liberals' defence of press freedom as liberal principle without a class critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional liberalism of Ploug and Lehmann; the sources do not state it directly.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement united Danes, Swedes and Norwegians as related peoples under constitutional states, not on a single-group franchise; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the internet did not exist and no position can be inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement had no view on open records beyond liberal publicity.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from Lutheran, liberal-minded Nordic societies of the time; the movement did not address marriage law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from its liberal base and cultural aim of unity; religious-minority boycotts have no place in the sources.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's National Liberal, constitutional-monarchist base, which favoured elected parliaments over selection by lot.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The movement was cultural and political, not religious; adherents (Lutheran state churches) had no common line on doctrinal reinterpretation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed by the cultural-political movement; its bourgeois-liberal base and Nordic welfare legacy point in different directions, so inferred as indifferent.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; mid-19th-century liberals and royal sympathisers held conventional views of military service, inferred from the era's norms.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement was loyal to its monarchies and shared Lutheran state churches, so promoting atheism is inferred to be foreign to it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Danish National Liberals and Bernadotte kings were establishment liberals and monarchists, so abolishing police and prisons is inferred as alien.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The political wing's confederation and personal-union proposals shared sovereignty among the Nordic kingdoms, from which a mild power-sharing preference is inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; liberal civil society favoured private initiative but the welfare legacy points the other way, so split.

term-limits.rationale: Never addressed; the National Liberals sought constitutional government and nothing on terms is documented, so indifferent.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic; a movement of constitutional liberals and kings would see representative, not delegated, government as the norm; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; inferred as indifferent.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Mid-19th-century Nordic state churches reserved office to men, and the movement did not challenge that; inferred from the era.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; Nordic family law later became egalitarian but nothing is attributed to the movement itself, so indifferent.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the liberal, cross-border Nordic tradition that grew from Scandinavism, whose legacy includes mutual rights for Nordic citizens (Helsinki Treaty); the movement itself did not address it.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the movement's bourgeois-liberal base; it had little economic or housing policy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: its literary and student networks were built on authors and publishers, and liberal 19th-century opinion defended intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the movement was a liberal student and literary one, not a drilled, state-run youth programme.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Nordic cooperation tradition it fed, whose states keep nuclear weapons off their soil in peacetime.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: the political wing wanted defence provided by a Nordic alliance of the kin states rather than by outside powers.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; a liberal inference that past mass killings should be acknowledged.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the liberal, meritocratic outlook of its National Liberal leaders.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: its political wing sought a military alliance against Russia and Prussia and urged Sweden-Norway to fight for Denmark in 1864.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Its whole case rested on a shared Old Norse heritage, mythology and kinship of the three peoples, though it treated them as kin peoples rather than one nation.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the conventional 19th-century view of sex as natural.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; the movement honoured the fallen of the 1848 and 1864 wars as patriots, but the Lutheran Nordic setting had no saint tradition.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: its liberal, secular-leaning politics were about alliance and culture, not a cosmic struggle of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; it concerned Nordic kin living in neighbouring states, not diasporas.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural Scandinavism through student meetings and literature came first and outlived the political wing, which failed in 1864.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from conventional Lutheran 19th-century religion.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from conventional 19th-century views of religion and gender.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: a liberal, cross-border movement favouring Nordic unity, not majority control of the economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: National Liberals sought to unify the kin peoples and to hold Schleswig within Denmark, favouring larger single units for a people.

independent-unions.rationale: Modern unions barely existed in the 1840s-60s and the movement had no labour policy.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Anachronistic; the bourgeois-liberal movement held no view on socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred from its bourgeois-liberal base.

second-chamber.rationale: The Danish National Liberals who led the political wing backed the 1849 constitution with two chambers; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: The bourgeois-liberal base favoured private property over communal ownership of production; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The political wing's confederation plans were between kingdoms, not towns; no view on local assemblies.

person-over-state.rationale: The National Liberals were constitutional liberals who valued individual rights against absolutism; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Cultural Scandinavism drew on Old Norse mythology and heritage, but the sources give no view on a spiritual side of politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The movement sought union of states and gave no view on revocable regional powers.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement rested on kinship of nations and shared culture, not on organising races to defend group interests; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Cultural Scandinavism celebrated a shared Old Norse ancestry and heritage as a source of pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The political wing aimed at a defensive alliance against Russia and Prussia; the 1863 promise to Denmark was for defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Scandinavism rested on the closely related languages, shared Old Norse heritage and history of Danes, Swedes and Norwegians as the basis for unity across state borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the movement's bourgeois-liberal National Liberal base, which favoured common national representation; religious electorates were not an issue.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the movement's origin as defence against Russia and Prussia, which threatened Denmark in particular, though a plot to partition is not documented.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed by a movement with little social policy; its student meetings were cultural, and its liberal base gives no clear answer.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; a 19th-century movement had no environmental policy to infer from.

future-generations.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement had no stated position on duties to future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from mid-19th-century bourgeois-liberal attitudes, which did not give women's values weight in politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: the political wing sought military alliance to defend against Russia and Prussia, so armaments reduction ran against its aim.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's dynastic diplomacy under Oscar I and Carl XV was partly private and partly public, so no clear stance can be inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from its liberal base and the 1873 Scandinavian monetary union, which favoured easy cross-border monetary exchange.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: a Nordic union under monarchs would rest on state armed forces.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the movement sought military alliance against Russia and Prussia, so refusing to fight cuts against it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; the movement had little social programme.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from its bourgeois-liberal base; tax credits are anachronistic.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; the 1873 monetary union was a later legacy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: the movement worked through monarchs, parliaments and student networks, not revolution.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; it had no economic programme, so it is neutral.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed and anachronistic; the movement had no view on valuing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Its romantic heritage rested on shared Norse culture, but it joined nations in a larger union rather than treating one nation as sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its liberal outlook.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stressed equals joining in union.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; its unity rested on shared language and heritage.

public-service-media.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its liberal, press-and-private-association base.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, whose unity rested on Old Norse heritage and language rather than religion.

farm-price-support.rationale: The movement had little economic policy; its bourgeois-liberal base gives no clear lean.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement predates nuclear arms and its defence aim was a collective alliance.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from its National Liberal, bourgeois base, which sought national and cross-class unity rather than class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the liberal outlook of its Danish National Liberal supporters.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its liberal outlook and the later Nordic legal harmonisation, which treated women as equals.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The movement treated Danes, Swedes and Norwegians as kin peoples with closely related but separate languages, not as one language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement held no position on pollution and its liberal base gives no clear lean.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its liberal constitutional outlook, with monarchs and parliaments but no formal customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; not a topic for a 19th-century unionist movement.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; the movement concerned union among the Nordic kin peoples, not immigration.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement had no labour policy, and its bourgeois-liberal base gives no clear lean.

voter-id.rationale: Anachronistic: voter identification was not an issue in the 1840s-60s and the movement took no position.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The movement was about Nordic unity and the Lutheran state churches were common to all three countries, so it took no line on religious precedence. Inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Its National Liberal wing sought constitutional and parliamentary government, but the movement itself was about union rather than the definition of democracy; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement never addressed sexual morality and its adherents' views are not documented.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The bourgeois-liberal base valued free expression and press, so state cutoffs would not fit; the technology is anachronistic. Inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: A 19th-century liberal movement had no concept of cash income support and favoured limited state welfare; inferred and anachronistic.

women-suffrage.rationale: The movement predates women's suffrage in all three countries and took no position; adherents' views are not documented.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The movement drew on shared heritage and Lutheran societies and did not regard religion as oppressing women; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic: its heritage appeal was cultural and linguistic and it took no stand on racial categories.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Anachronistic: no equality agencies existed and the movement had no social policy; the later Nordic equality tradition is a legacy only.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the bourgeois-liberal base of the National Liberals; the movement had no stated position on land claims.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic: international criminal courts did not exist, and the movement's alliance plans give no basis for a side.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the movement was romantic and cultural, drawing on Old Norse myth rather than scripture, though its supporters lived within Lutheran state churches.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Anachronistic: Indigenous and gendered self-rule guarantees were not mid-19th-century concerns, so no side can be inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: mid-19th-century liberal nationalists were market-minded property defenders and a planned state is far outside their outlook.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the National Liberals pushed for constitutional government and popular representation, and the sources give no preference for indirect election.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: Scandinavists belonged to Lutheran state-church societies and sought no disestablishment, though the sources are silent on it.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: Danish National Liberals sought a unified Danish state up to the Eider and resisted separate status for Schleswig's German-speaking majority areas.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: the Danish National Liberals backed the Eider border claim, and the union plans were set by dynasts and elites, not by local votes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement predates decolonisation and says nothing about colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: a bourgeois, urban, trade-minded movement had no ideal of limited needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the sources never mention Sami or other indigenous peoples; the era's liberal nationalism favoured free settlement and state authority.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: mid-19th-century liberal nationalism took male-only conscription for granted, as Nordic military alliance plans did.

missingStatements.text: The Nordic countries should be united in a political union or confederation under a common crown.
missingStatements.rationale: The political wing's aim ranged from confederation to union under one king, not captured by the kin-peoples statement because it names the form of union.

missingStatements.text: Small states should join together to protect themselves against a large neighbouring power.
missingStatements.rationale: Threats from Russia and Prussia were decisive in drawing Nordic states together, and Denmark's isolation in 1864 is the movement's defining failure.

missingStatements.text: A shared ancient heritage, mythology and literature should be taught and celebrated across neighbouring countries as a basis for cooperation.
missingStatements.rationale: Cultural Scandinavism promoted Old Norse mythology, a common literary heritage and joint societies and periodicals.

notes: Political Scandinavism (union plans) and cultural Scandinavism (heritage, language, student meetings) differ; cultural answers are the more durable. No true primary text was opened: s5 is a Wikipedia summary of a 1962 treaty, so stated positions rest on secondary sources. Dating of Andersen's poem is disputed (1837 or 1839).
